flashcard_questions.q: What is the break-even point for a business?
flashcard_questions.a: The output level where total revenue exactly equals total costs, so there is neither profit nor loss.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the formula for the break-even level of output?
flashcard_questions.a: Fixed costs ÷ (Selling price − Variable cost per unit).

flashcard_questions.q: Contribution per unit = Selling price − ____ per unit.
What does contribution per unit tell a business?
flashcard_questions.a: How much money from each sale goes towards covering fixed costs.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the formula for margin of safety?
What is the contribution per unit when a product sells for £450 and costs £280 per unit to make?
What is the break-even output when fixed costs are £25,000 and contribution per unit is £170?
What is the margin of safety when actual sales are 425 units and the break-even point is 250 units?
Why must a break-even answer in units always be rounded up?
flashcard_questions.a: Rounding down would leave the business short of covering its costs.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to the break-even point if fixed costs rise?
flashcard_questions.a: It moves to the right, so more units must be sold to cover costs.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to the break-even point if variable costs fall?
flashcard_questions.a: It moves to the left, so fewer units need to be sold.

flashcard_questions.q: What happens to the margin of safety when the selling price is increased?
flashcard_questions.a: It increases, because the revenue line crosses total costs sooner.

flashcard_questions.q: On a break-even diagram, what does the area to the left of the crossing point represent?
flashcard_questions.a: The business is making a loss.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does the total costs line on a break-even diagram start above zero?
flashcard_questions.a: Fixed costs still have to be paid at zero output.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the drawback for Meringue bakery of using cheaper ingredients to lower break-even?
flashcard_questions.a: Lower quality could damage its reputation and lead to fewer sales.

notes: 15 cards: 3 term→definition, 2 formula (stated verbatim), 1 cloze on contribution, 3 one-step calculations using the lesson's own figures (£450/£280, £25,000/£170, 425/250), 5 change→effect facts, 1 case-study drawback (Meringue). Dropped 'break-even analysis' as a separate glossary card — it overlaps the break-even definition and would interfere.
